recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change ElementDefinition.constraint.human to markdown unless FHIR-I explicitly reopens and reverses the plain-string constraint-message decision; use rendering-markdown for richer display and track any remaining IG Publisher behavior in the IG Publisher repository rather than core FHIR source.
issue_request: FHIR-25392 asked to change ElementDefinition.constraint.human from string to markdown so human-readable constraint messages could contain rich text, and to update IG Publisher rendering. It was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification: FHIR-I rejected a core markdown datatype change for constraint messages and recommended the existing rendering-markdown extension instead.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged FHIR-25392 source-changing commit was found in the core checkout. That absence is consistent with the resolution because the authoritative ElementDefinition source still defines ElementDefinition.constraint.human as string, while the optional rendering-markdown extension exists outside the core datatype model.
additional_context: FHIR-28141 later created an apparent conflict by mentioning ElementDefinition.constraint.human in its resolution, but its Jira title/description concerned ElementDefinition.constraint.requirements. The Jira-tagged implementation commit a74d790b4480099fb9d8b68ad2df3bef4844d99b changed constraint.requirements, binding.description, and mapping.comment to markdown, not constraint.human. FHIR-I minutes on 2022-08-29 and Zulip discussion concluded that FHIR-28141 had a resolution typo and both FHIR-25392 and FHIR-28141 were already applied correctly; FHIR-28141 is already represented on the combined branch by commit 5c79968c33331c2855000b45df47f2ff006c12bc.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active, normative ElementDefinition source in source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml already keeps ElementDefinition.constraint.human as string, matching the seed decision and later clarification. The Extension Pack rendering-markdown definition applies to string elements and carries markdown content, so rich rendering does not require changing the core datatype.

related_jiras.note: Later ElementDefinition markdown issue in the same family; FHIR-I clarified its resolution typo should not override the FHIR-25392 decision to keep constraint.human as string.
